subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu direct session can become unusable after /reset or /new and fall back to generic 'Something went wrong...' while session index points to missing transcript IDs

question: For direct-chat `/reset` and `/new`, should OpenClaw block publication of the new session mapping until a durable transcript exists, or allow publication with an explicit repair/remap fallback?
rationale: Both approaches can fix the reported missing-transcript lineage, but they differ in user-visible reset semantics and recovery behavior, and current labels already request maintainer/product review before a new fix PR.

options.title: Transactional rotation
options.body: Create or prewarm the new transcript before updating the session store or lineage, keeping the previous transcript authoritative if creation fails.

options.title: Repair-after-publication
options.body: Allow the mapping to advance but immediately detect missing transcript files and remap to the newest valid family member with a specific recovery message.

options.title: Close into broader UX work
options.body: Treat the missing transcript as a subset of broader Feishu failure translation work and leave only #89247 as canonical.

recommendation.title: Transactional rotation
recommendation.body: Create or prewarm the new transcript before updating the session store or lineage, keeping the previous transcript authoritative if creation fails.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history on reply session initialization guard and lifecycle storage seams.
